record.original_question: Let u be a ﬁxed point of a primitive morphism. Then the language of u is closed under reversal if and only if u is palindromic.

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Let $A$ be a finite alphabet and $\varphi : A^* \to A^*$ a morphism. Recall that $\varphi$ is called primitive if there exists an integer $k \ge 1$ such that, for every pair of letters $a, b \in A$, the letter $a$ occurs in $\varphi^k(b)$. An infinite word $u \in A^{\mathbb{N}}$ is a fixed point of $\varphi$ if $\varphi(u) = u$. The language $\mathcal{L}(u)$ of $u$ is the set of all finite factors (contiguous subwords) of $u$. The reversal of a finite word $w = w_1 w_2 \cdots w_n$ is $\widetilde{w} = w_n \cdots w_2 w_1$, and a word $w$ is a palindrome if $w = \widetilde{w}$. The language $\mathcal{L}(u)$ is said to be closed under reversal if $\widetilde{w} \in \mathcal{L}(u)$ whenever $w \in \mathcal{L}(u)$. Finally, the infinite word $u$ is called palindromic if $\mathcal{L}(u)$ contains infinitely many distinct palindromes.

Prove or disprove: if $u$ is a fixed point of a primitive morphism, then $\mathcal{L}(u)$ is closed under reversal if and only if $u$ is palindromic.
artifact.status_search_result: This is closely related to the Hof–Knill–Simon (HKS) question on palindromic substitutive sequences. One implication (palindromic ⇒ closed under reversal) is straightforward, while the converse is the subject of active research. Labbé (2014) provided a counterexample to a related question of Hof, Knill and Simon, indicating that statements of this kind require additional hypotheses. The exact equivalence as stated remains open in full generality, with positive results known in restricted settings (e.g. binary alphabet, marked morphisms).

status_evidence.title: A Counterexample to a Question of Hof, Knill and Simon
status_evidence.snippet: Labbé constructs a counterexample to the HKS question on palindromic substitutive sequences.
status_evidence.claim: Closely related question of Hof–Knill–Simon has counterexamples, indicating subtleties in the equivalence.

status_evidence.title: Palindromic sequences generated from marked morphisms
status_evidence.snippet: Studies palindromic fixed points of marked primitive morphisms.
status_evidence.claim: Partial results known for restricted classes of primitive morphisms.

status_evidence.title: On the Zero Defect Conjecture
status_evidence.snippet: Discusses palindromic defect of fixed points of primitive morphisms; counterexamples on ternary alphabet, valid on binary.
status_evidence.claim: Related conjectures on palindromicity of primitive-morphism fixed points are open or only partially resolved.
